string-array.name: legal_imprint_texts
string-array.item:
Ordo is free and open source. The app is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. It comes without warranty, as far as the law allows.

Source code: https://github.com/BEKO2210/ordo

Ordo is based on “Material Files” by Hai Zhang.
I do not take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board and am not obliged to.

string-array.name: legal_privacy_texts
string-array.item: Ordo collects no data about you. The app has no ads, no tracking and no analytics. Your files stay on your device. Ordo never connects to the internet on its own.

Belkis Aslani
Vogelsangstraße 32
71691 Freiberg am Neckar
Germany
Email: nullmesh@protonmail.com

Ordo only asks for what a file manager needs:

• Access to all files: show, copy, move, rename and delete files.
• See installed apps: show the app overview and open files with the right app.
• Install and remove apps: only when you start it in Ordo.
• Internet and Wi-Fi state: only for servers you set up and for the built-in FTP server.
• Notifications and background service: long tasks keep running and show their progress.
• Fingerprint or screen lock: Android does the check. Ordo only learns whether it succeeded.
• Shortcuts: only when you add one to your home screen.

Ordo stores data only on your device: your settings, bookmarks and the sign-in details of servers you set up. Deleted files stay in the folder “.OrdoTrash” on the same storage, usually for 30 days.

Ordo sends none of this to me or to anyone else. If Android backup is switched on, Android saves Ordo's settings to your Google account. The vault is excluded.

When you uninstall Ordo, Android deletes the app data on the device.

Ordo encrypts files in the vault with AES-256 and keeps them in the app\'s protected storage. The key stays in your device\'s keystore and never leaves it.\n\nImportant: If you uninstall Ordo or clear its app data, the files in the vault are lost. Take them out or back them up first.

A backup is a ZIP file in the place you choose, for example on a USB drive. If you want, Ordo encrypts it with your password (AES-256). Ordo does not store the password.\n\nIf you choose cloud storage such as Google Drive, that provider\'s app transfers the file. The provider\'s privacy policy applies.

When you set up a server (FTP, SFTP, SMB or WebDAV), Ordo connects to it directly. The server\'s operator sees your IP address and the files you transfer. Nobody else is involved.\n\nThe built-in FTP server only runs while you have it switched on.

When you download Ordo from Google Play, Google processes data under its own rules: https://policies.google.com/privacy\n\nGoogle only gives me summarised figures, such as installs and crash reports if you allowed them in Android. I cannot identify anyone from them.

The Ordo website is hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). When you open it, GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver and protect the site. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. GitHub also processes data in the USA and relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses.

The site sets no cookies and loads nothing from other providers.

More: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement
When you email me, I process your address and your message in order to reply (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). I delete them once your request is settled. My email provider is Proton AG in Switzerland.

You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20) and objection (Art. 21). Email me to use them.

You can also complain to a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). The one responsible for me is the State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of Baden-Württemberg: https://www.baden-wuerttemberg.datenschutz.de

Because Ordo sends no data to me, I hold no data about you from the app.
14 November 2026. I update this text when the app changes. The German version is the binding one.
